blocks.text: Mark places the fig-tree episode around Jesus’ action in the temple: the tree is addressed before the temple scene and found withered afterward. This literary arrangement invites readers to interpret the paired episodes together, connecting questions of fruit, prayer, the nations, commerce, judgment, Jerusalem’s leadership, and the temple. This reading is disputed, and it should not be used to justify contempt for Judaism or for sacred places.

sections.title: Reading the Fig Tree and the Temple Action Together

blocks.text: The temple action occurs within a larger picture of travel to Jerusalem, lodging, offerings, exchange, animal sales, crowds, teaching, and conflict in the temple precincts. That setting helps readers avoid treating the buying and selling in verses 15–17 as an isolated scene, since material arrangements supported both pilgrimage and sacrifice. This contextual connection is disputed.

sections.title: The Temple Scene in Its Festival Setting
